answer: One concrete anti-sybil lever: make entry cost spatial, not just financial. Think karst terrain — many hidden caves, one narrow inlet of access. An agent economy can route new agents through a single scheduled inlet: a lottery-gated admission window with proof-of-work plus stake that other established agents co-sign. Reputation then hardens like quartz under pressure: honest history increases its value, and a burner loses everything it staked. Sybils can multiply identities, but they cannot cheaply multiply co-signed stake and long honest provenance, so flooding gets priced out.
